q: What is StudyLamb, and who is Professor Lamby?
a: StudyLamb is a study app that turns your own class materials into flashcards, practice questions, and audio lessons. Professor Lamby is the friendly sheep mascot who shows up on the welcome screen and loading screens.

q: What is a class in StudyLamb?
a: A class is a folder for one school subject, like Science or Math. You give it a name and a color, and it can hold as many exams as you like.

q: How do you create a new class?
a: On the Your classes page, tap New class, type a name like Science or Math, pick a color, and tap Create. StudyLamb then walks you into adding your first exam.

q: How do you add an exam to a class?
a: Open the class and tap New exam. Give the exam a name, then add your study materials. One class can hold many exams, like Unit 1 test and Final.

q: What kinds of files can you upload as study materials?
a: PDFs, photos of pages, Word documents ending in .docx, plain text files, and text you paste in. Each file can be up to 25 megabytes. There is also a camera button that opens your camera straight away.

q: What does StudyLamb do after you upload materials?
a: It reads the pages and builds a study set: chapters or sections, flashcards, practice questions, and podcast episodes, all from your own material.

q: What is a syllabus upload?
a: On the classes page, Upload a syllabus lets you send your course syllabus. StudyLamb reads it and creates your classes and their major exams for you, with dates when the syllabus lists them.

q: When materials disagree, which one wins?
a: Chapter material from the textbook or teacher is the source of truth. If a student's own notes contradict it, only the true version goes into the study guide.

q: What happens when the same fact appears in many of your notes?
a: StudyLamb treats it as important and gives it more weight, so it shows up more often in your cards and questions.

q: What happens if you upload the exact same file twice?
a: StudyLamb detects that the file is identical to one already processed and skips it, so you never pay or wait for the same work twice.

q: Can you rename or delete classes, exams, and chapters?
a: Yes. Everything you can add, you can edit or delete. Use the pencil to rename and the trash to delete, on the classes page for classes and exams, and on the exam home page for chapters.

q: What is the final review, and how do you build one?
a: At the end of a semester, tap Final review: pick classes on the classes page, check the classes on your final, and tap Build final review. StudyLamb combines all their flashcards and practice questions into one review exam, free of charge.

q: Which tab is first in the bottom bar?
a: Home is the first tab. It shows your exam's progress, daily goal, due date, sample exam, and your notes and uploads.

q: What do the colors of the app mean?
a: Blue screens are for learning, red-tinted screens are for quizzing and recall, and green marks a correct answer. The same color means the same thing on every screen.

q: What wording does StudyLamb use when you miss an answer?
a: It says Not yet and tells you what to try next, instead of words like wrong or failed. It praises your strategy and effort, like That checklist trick worked.

q: How do flashcards decide what to show you?
a: Spaced repetition. Cards you know well come back later as quick review, and cards you struggle with come back sooner and more often, on every page of the app.

q: How do you study a flashcard?
a: Read the question, say or think the answer, then tap the card to flip it and check. Grade yourself honestly so the schedule learns what you know.

q: What does the flashcard audio button do?
a: It reads the card aloud using your device's own voice. As it reads, the current word is highlighted and a little ball bounces from word to word, so you can follow along.

q: Does flashcard audio cost BrainBucks?
a: No. It uses your device's built-in speech, so listening is free and works offline once the page is loaded.

q: Can you draw on study cards?
a: Yes. You can sketch right on a card, and the ink is slightly transparent so the card's words stay easy to read underneath.

q: What is the Memorize game?
a: Memorize shows an answer with the first letter of each word, and you type the words. It runs in three rounds so tricky words get extra practice.

q: What counts as passing a Memorize round?
a: Your accuracy must be strictly above ninety percent. Typing a neighboring keyboard key by accident still counts as a match.

q: What happens when you type a wrong letter in Memorize?
a: You find out right away: the word turns red, you see which key you pressed, and the card shows the correct word so you can keep going and fix it.

q: What are the two podcast modes on the Listen tab?
a: Q and A plays every question and answer in order, like an audio quiz. Abstract tells the topic as a fun, memorable audio lesson with stories and memory tricks.

q: Which tab is the Listen tab, and why first?
a: Listen is the first study tab inside an exam, so you can start learning hands-free right away, for example on the way to school.

q: How do you close the podcast player bar?
a: Tap the close button on the mini-player at the bottom of the screen and it disappears.

q: What is on the exam Home page?
a: Your progress and daily goal, the due date box, sample exam, add materials, the chapters list with rename pencils, what you uploaded, and your personal notes.

q: What are the two kinds of notes on Home?
a: What you uploaded shows your original files word for word, and My notes holds your own typed or spoken notes. You can add more with the Upload and Camera buttons.

q: Can you add spoken notes?
a: Yes. Record a voice note and StudyLamb transcribes it into text for you. Transcribing a new spoken note costs one BrainBuck.

q: How does the daily goal work?
a: Each exam shows a goal like fifteen reviews a day, and the header chip counts you up, like eight of twenty done. Small visible wins keep you going.

q: What is the Practice tab?
a: Practice asks you questions from your materials with immediate feedback. Things you struggle with come up more often, just like flashcards.

q: How does a sample exam work?
a: Open Sample exam, pick five, ten, twenty, or all questions, and answer them. After each answer you check the model answer and tap Got it or Not yet.

q: What can you do after finishing a sample exam?
a: You see your percentage, and if you missed any, one tap starts a retake with only the not-yet questions, so you practice exactly what needs work.

q: Do missed sample exam questions affect the rest of the app?
a: Yes. Questions you missed come back more often in Cards and Practice, so every page helps you fix the same gaps.

q: How do you set a due date for an exam?
a: On the exam Home page, use the When is it due box. Choose Test, Exam, or Homework, pick the date, and StudyLamb plans your studying around it.

q: What is the difference between cram mode and spread mode?
a: If the due date is about three days away or less, cram mode teaches you more in less time by putting unknown cards first. With more time, StudyLamb spreads new cards into small daily sets plus review.

q: Are there timers in StudyLamb?
a: Timers are off by default. There are no countdowns and no streaks, so you can focus on learning instead of the clock.

q: What are BrainBucks?
a: BrainBucks are the app's coins, shown with a dollar bill icon. Anything that uses AI, like building a study set or making an episode, costs BrainBucks.

q: How much do common AI actions cost?
a: Building a study set costs five BrainBucks plus one per PDF or photo, a podcast episode costs three, and a new read-aloud clip or spoken note costs one. Replaying audio that already exists is always free.

q: How many BrainBucks do new students get?
a: Every student starts with twenty five free BrainBucks, and the balance chip shows at the top of the classes and exam pages.

q: What happens when your BrainBucks run low?
a: At five or fewer you get a reminder to top up soon. If an action would spend almost all of your balance, a pop up warns you and suggests cheaper options, like converting to PDF or doing one chapter at a time. You can still go ahead.

q: What if you run out of BrainBucks in the middle of a task?
a: You get a small grace buffer of three BrainBucks so the task can finish its current step. Past that, the task pauses, and topping up lets it continue.

q: What happens to your BrainBucks if an AI task fails?
a: Failed work is never billed. If something goes wrong, the BrainBucks for that task are refunded automatically.

q: What is the Dyslexia setting?
a: It turns on structured literacy support: explicit sound letter and spelling patterns, guided practice in the Word Lab, and instant feedback, on top of clear fonts and spacing.

q: What is the ADHD setting?
a: It shapes studying into short chunks with immediate feedback, visible progress, goal setting, and an easy low-friction start, so getting going takes less effort.

q: How does read aloud work in StudyLamb?
a: Read aloud is a toggle you can turn on when you want it, not a replacement for reading. You can also adjust text size and spacing in Settings.
